newsitem.title: USA: PSA upbeat about "Education Zone" tax credit plan.
newsitem.headline: PSA upbeat about "Education Zone" tax credit plan.

text.p: A key spokesman for bond dealers said Friday that a new pilot plan to give $400 million in tax credits to banks making infrastructure loans to public schools is not a threat to the muni market and is worth study.

"It's a very creative idea that is worth study by the community," Micah Green, executive vice president of PSA The Bond Market Trade Association, said in a telephone interview about the new "Education Zones" initiative.
"The volume of school construction bonds exceeds $10 billion a year. This is not going to supplant the need to issue traditional tax-exempt bonds," Green said.
Green was talking about a provision included in the mammoth tax bill passed by the U.S. Congress on Thursday and headed for signature by President Clinton.

Sponsored by Rep. Charles Rangel, D-N.Y., the plan would make $400 million in interest-free capital available annually for the next two years to localities to improve public and secondary schools in empowerment zones, enterprise community and other areas where at least 35 percent of students are poor.
Localities could borrow money from lenders for school repair or renovation, equipment purchases, course material or teacher training, according to a bill summary.
"The proposal provides a tax credit to the lender in an amount equal to the interest that would otherwise be paid by the local government," the summary says.
"The term of the borrowing is set so that the net benefit to the school is 50 percent of the borrowed amount," the summary says.
A school would "partner" with private businesses that would make contributions to the school in the form of goods, expertise, training or services, the summary says.
State education agencies would allocate their states' shares of the $400 million pot to localities, the summary says.
"We're taking the same success of the Empowerment Zones to another level - public schools," Rangel said in a statement.
"This is a perfect marriage that will help more kids qualify for college and support our public schools through partnerships with the private sector," Rangel continued.
Green said, "We have to study it and try to make it work because the needs in school construction are so great."
"Our desire is to help reduce the cost of public services through the capital markets," Green continued.
"Tax-exempt bonds are a vehicle for doing that. But if new ideas come up, before casting negative judgment on them, we should give them a chance to play out," he said.
